claims.text: A generated two-account case imported as one case (synth.to_case) gives, through overrides.case_figures and combined_figures, every line's category under its case line id, every money-in bucket (M2, M19-M25) with its evidence, M17, M18 and every per-account indicator exactly as truth.case says (P17), for every archetype and profile and for several feature sets, seeds and lengths; and the same cases satisfy P11: each pair is one debit and one credit of equal amount in different accounts, each naming the other, no line in two pairs, the pairs equal the generator's moves, every own-account transfer is half of a pair, no debit is left with two candidates, and M17 - M19 equals the generator's money from outside the accounts.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m invariants tests/test_synth_case.py -k 'p17 or p11'

claims.text: Contracts: to_case imports both accounts with the generated profile (directors, own accounts, VAT stagger, demo, label) and the workspace summary shows both accounts, combined figures and no possible own-account transfer; a single-account feature set has no case truth and its truth file has no 'case' key; `cma generate --feature all --case` makes the case and writes the case truth.
The existing synth tests, the byte-identity check of existing archetypes and profiles included, still pass.

claims.proof_cmd: ruff check src tests evals; python evals/run_evals.py >/dev/null; echo evals=$?

notes: Commit 8a7aa78 on bridgie-task/statement-review/T35. synth.Truth gains `case` (set only with two_accounts; left out of the truth file otherwise, so non-featured and single-account truth files are unchanged): accounts, category_by_id by case line id (key:id), own_account_pairs (debit first, worked out from the generator's own moves by day and amount, not from the categoriser), combined buckets and cash deposits, outside_money_in (credits that are half of no move) and per-account indicators. synth.to_case(rows, truth, work) makes one demo case in the store; `cma generate --case` calls it. In the case the generator's moves are settled by the pairing (precedence above the profile name), so categories match T10's per-account truth while rule ids become pairing:...; the full-suite run was taken before the README edit and a one-line test lint fix (unused variable renamed), both re-checked by ruff and the targeted test runs above.
